_meta: Machinevertaling (nl naar en) van de eigen factcheck kabul-beelden-turkije van Factiz, eigen werk van de redactie (B82, B84), door claude-sonnet-5-5, eigenvertaling-v1; doublecheck/eigenvertaling.py, PLAN #37.8.

velden.kop: Video of an Apache and a C-17 was filmed in Kabul in 2021, not in Turkey
velden.oordeel_zin: The footage is from Kabul airport on August 16, 2021, and in September 2026 the US Air Force was still at Incirlik [1] [3].
velden.bewering: American cargo planes are taking everything away from the air force base in Turkey and leaving for good.
velden.kort: On August 27 a video circulated on X of American aircraft supposedly leaving a base in Turkey for good [4]. The footage is from August 16, 2021, at Kabul airport, where an Apache helicopter drove people away from a C-17 [1] [2]. In September the US Air Force was still reporting regular activity at Incirlik base in Turkey [3] [6].
velden.tekst:
On Thursday, August 27 at 7:04 p.m., a Dutch-language account on X posted a 37-second video [4]. The text says that American cargo planes are bringing equipment and supplies from "the air force base in Turkey" back to the United States and leaving the base completely [4]. The post does not say which base [4]. As of November 18 it had been viewed 9,252 times [4].

The same claim appeared eight hours earlier in English on X, at 11:15 a.m., with a video of the same length [5]. That post was viewed 685,711 times [5]. The Dutch text looks like a translation of it [4] [5].

The footage is five years old. It comes from Kabul airport on Monday, August 16, 2021, in the days of the American evacuation from Afghanistan [1] [2]. Large groups of Afghans had walked onto the runway around a C-17 that was taxiing [1]. A US Army Apache helicopter flew low over the ground to drive them away [1] [2]. The War Zone put the video online the same day, with a social media post as its source [1]. The Aviationist described the scene a day later [2].

So the video says nothing about Turkey in 2026 [1] [4]. A C-17 is a large transport aircraft of the US Air Force; that type flew the airlift out of Kabul in 2021 [2].

Nor did the Americans leave Turkey. On September 18 and 19, service members of the 39th Air Base Wing at Incirlik base held a 24-hour remembrance for prisoners of war and those missing in action [3]. On September 25, the same unit reopened a building with rooms for service members there, after a renovation of 949 days [6]. Both reports come from the US armed forces themselves [3] [6].
velden.niet_weten: We do not know who first linked the footage to Turkey. The oldest post with that explanation that we found is the English one of August 27 at 11:15 a.m. We also do not know who filmed the video in 2021. Whether anything changed in August 2026 regarding American troops in Turkey, we did not investigate further; the two September reports we read say nothing about a departure.
nog_uitzoeken: Whether there was news at the end of August 2026 about American troops in Turkey that could explain the post.
tijdlijn: At Kabul airport an Apache drives people away from a C-17; The War Zone puts the video online [1].
The Aviationist describes the same scene [2].
An English post presents the video as Americans leaving a base in Turkey [5].
The Dutch post with the same claim [4].
At Incirlik a renovated building with rooms for service members reopens [6].
beeld_bijschrift: The War Zone, August 16, 2021: an Apache drives Afghans away from a C-17 at Kabul airport.
beeld_alt: Still from the video: a helicopter low over a runway next to a large transport aircraft. Stamp: FALSE.
The video at The War Zone of an Apache helicopter above the Kabul runway, next to a C-17.
